mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to 60-day S&P 500 forward returns: lower rates predict positive returns, as low rates extend the duration of equity cash flows and compress discount rates.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and 60-day returns show no significant inverse correlation (p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 225, indicating high inflation, 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative due to central bank tightening and reduced equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 225 and 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 225) triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns, as the dual pressure of monetary tightening and inflation erodes equity valuations.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL>225) does not yield negative returns in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 9.0%), 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative due to weak economic growth and reduced corporate earnings visibility.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 9.0 and 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 500,000 units, 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative as weak housing activity signals broader economic weakness and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: HOUST < 500 and 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low housing starts (HOUST < 500) and low residential fixed investment (RSAFS < 350,000) signals a deteriorating housing market, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: HOUST < 500 and RSAFS < 350000 and 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 90, 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative due to declining manufacturing output and reduced business investment.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 90 and 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 225, 5-day S&P 500 returns are negative due to immediate market reactions to high inflation, including central bank policy expectations and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 225 and 5-day returns are not negative in > 60% of triggered instances.
